cases.why: CLOSED 2026-09-15, vernacular-surface wave: the literate `Statement:` grammar grew `forall x : T, body` (and ∀). The sort is mandatory. A named `Pi` reifies as the `Forall` shape the elimination rules speak, and an ordinary tactic is handed the body with the prenex binders discharged as eigenvariables — ∀-introduction, which is the reading this surface already gives every free variable.

Lean has one elaborator and one proof object per theorem; LOGOS ships a second certified engine (the incremental grid solver) that the general backward chainer cannot match on finite-domain premises, and selects it structurally from the premise shape rather than from a flag or a keyword. We defend that: BOTH routes pass the identical kernel door, so the trust level is unchanged and no theorem becomes provable that was not entailed — the fast path is the only reason a logic-grid puzzle certifies in a browser with no Z3 at all, in milliseconds instead of a depth-100 saturation that never returns. Lean's analogue would be a hand-written `decide`-style tactic the author must name explicitly, which is strictly worse for the mathematician who did not know to ask. What the divergence genuinely costs is proof-SHAPE stability: adding one `every X is A or B` or one `exactly one X is A` premise flips the whole theorem from `UniversalInst`/`ModusPonens` over the quantified originals to `DisjunctionElim`/`Contradiction` over grounded ones, and the grid route proves a premise set augmented with at-most-one, definite-description and functionality lemmas rather than the premises as written (all entailed, so still sound). The test pins exactly that — same text, same verdict, two structurally different certificates through the two public entry points — so a harness that snapshots rendered trees knows it is measuring premise structure it did not choose.
